headline: The machines
rest today.
metaldock.reading: Kanya Sankranti, when the sun crosses into Virgo. The tools are cleaned, garlanded and left alone. In the Rig Veda the maker of all is likened to a smith and a carpenter.
metaldock.caption:
The machines rest today.

Vishwakarma Puja falls on Kanya Sankranti, when the sun crosses into Virgo — one of the few Indian festivals that follows the sun rather than the moon, which is why it lands on 17 September almost every year.

The name is two Sanskrit words: vishva, all the world, and karman, the making. In the Rig Veda the maker of all is likened to a smith and a carpenter — which is to say the trade is honouring one of its own.

The tools are cleaned, garlanded and left unused for the day.
